answers.q1: There is a visible grounding mechanism: each メモ item shows a speaker name, a timestamp, and an expandable quoted original line with a 原文 (source) link, which reads as 'grounded in the meeting' rather than a free guess. But looking closely, the item labeled 'Ken・10:42' quotes 「Windows はいつ出しますか。」 — that line was actually said by Sarah at 10:30 per the transcript on the right, not by Ken at 10:42. So the UI announces grounding but the specific attribution shown is internally inconsistent, which would confuse anyone who actually checks it.
answers.q2: I'd click the 原文 › link right under the quoted line inside the メモ card — it's the most explicit 'go see the source' affordance on screen.
answers.q3: Yes for the top-level surfaces: the highlighted line under the title shows 'Ken' as speaker, each メモ card shows a name and time (e.g. '10:42 Ken'), and the 文字起こし panel lists every line with a timestamp and speaker. So attribution is visible without extra clicks — though as noted in q1, one attribution doesn't match its quoted text.
answers.q4: The '直す' (fix) link sitting directly beneath the quoted original text in each メモ card is the obvious correction entry point.
answers.q5: Moderately uneasy. The visible bullet has a name/time/quote trail, which helps, but 決まったこと and やること both show placeholder 'waiting...' text, so the doc reads as unfinished, and the one populated citation I could check didn't line up with its speaker — that would make me want to double-check everything else before forwarding it.

weaknesses.what: The メモ card credited to 'Ken・10:42' quotes 「Windows はいつ出しますか。」, which the transcript shows was actually said by Sarah at 10:30 — the grounding UI exists but the attached evidence doesn't match its claimed speaker/time.
weaknesses.fix: Guarantee the quoted 原文 snippet always comes from the exact speaker+timestamp shown on the card, or display the full Q&A exchange so it's clear whose words are whose.
